text:
Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed as attacks keep traffic down. The Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed, with ongoing attacks and mine threats keeping vessel transits at minimal levels [R1][R2][R3]. No material change; the corridor remained closed as in the prior read of 2026-10-08 [R4]. Heavy explosions and reports of possible mines in the southern passage signal a continued interdiction risk that deters carriers from attempting transits [R1][R5]. A crude oil tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, illustrating the threat of direct attacks on vessels in the strait [R2]. Iran’s IRGC commander reaffirmed that Hormuz security is a “red line” and will not be compromised, reinforcing Iran’s intent to keep the waterway under its control [R6]. Diplomatic statements that Iran could reopen the strait within a week have not been matched by any reported increase in actual transits, so the closure persists despite political talk [R7][R8]. Traffic data show only seven tankers crossed on Tuesday, far below the average and indicating that the corridor remains minimally used [R3]. What would change the assessment: A credible report of a sustained rise in verified vessel transits (e.g., AIS or port‐call data showing >50 % of pre‐war traffic) would overturn the assessment; the reporting does not currently collect raw AIS data. Transit volume drop: confirmed low crossings (only seven tankers) indicating a drop in traffic [R3]. Corridor attack or seizure: multiple recent attacks and possible mining incidents [R1][R2][R5]. Major rerouting declared: not observed. War‐risk or freight cost move: not observed. Transit closure or ban: not observed. Downstream production halt: not observed.
